title: Apricot Flan
description: Not just dessert — this is the one that makes the room go quiet. Soft custard, buttery pastry, and apricots that know their job.

method.instruction: Combine 200 g plain flour, 50 g white sugar, and 50 g ground almonds in a bowl. Rub in 125 g cold, cubed butter with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs, then bind together into a smooth pastry dough. Wrap in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.

Roll the chilled pastry dough out on a lightly floured surface and use it to line a loose-bottomed flan tin. Blind bake in a preheated oven at 180°C until lightly golden, then remove from the oven and allow to cool completely.

Separate the 2 eggs (reserve the whites for another use). In a heatproof bowl, beat the 2 egg yolks with the remaining 50 g white sugar and 1 tsp vanilla extract until pale. Gradually whisk in 250 ml of warm milk, then cook the mixture gently over a double boiler, stirring constantly, until thickened into a smooth custard. Remove from the heat, allow to cool slightly, then whip 150 ml pure cream to soft peaks and gently fold it through the custard.
Fill the cooled pastry shell with the prepared cream custard. Arrange the 6–8 halved apricots cut-side down over the surface of the custard.

Warm 3 tbsp apricot jam with 1 tbsp brandy in a small saucepan over low heat, then brush this glaze generously over the apricots. Finish by scattering the remaining 30 g flaked almonds over the top and chill the flan in the refrigerator until set.

notes.title: Make-Ahead
notes.content: The pastry shell can be baked a day in advance. Assemble the flan on the day of serving to keep the base crisp.

notes.title: Brandy
notes.content: To retain alcohol content, remove the pan from heat before adding. If the recipe calls for flambéing, that's intentional — but for sauces and braises where you want the flavour without burning off the alcohol, keep the heat low and never boil after adding.
